name: Off-Road Vehicle
description: A motorized vehicle not designed for highway use and capable of cross-country travel over natural terrain, such as an electric dirt bike. Alabama sets no power or speed limit for it and has no off-highway sticker for two-wheelers, but one of model year 2026 or later must be titled. Defined by Code of Alabama §32-12A-1 and, for title, §32-8-2 as amended by Act 2024-190.

restrictions.rule: Not designed for highway use and capable of cross-country travel over land, snow, ice, marsh or other natural terrain
No limit on motor power or speed

For title, an off-road vehicle is one not built to federal motor vehicle safety standards; one of model year 2026 or later must be titled, starting January 1, 2026, and none more than 10 model years old is titled

Alabama's voluntary three-year registration sticker covers only all-terrain vehicles (three or more non-highway tires) and recreational off-highway vehicles (four or more), not a two-wheeled off-road motorcycle
Alabama law sets no statewide minimum age, helmet or safety-course rule for riding one off the highway
Since October 1, 2025, can't be ridden in a creek, stream or other waterway, or on land under navigable or non-navigable waters, except on land the rider owns or has permission to use (Act 2025-429)
Barred from the Gulf of Mexico beaches and sand dunes off public roads, parking places and private driveways
On a public road a two-wheeled one is held to the motorcycle rules: a license tag, a Class M license and a helmet
